title.zh: 卷一百八十七上 列傳第一百三十七上: 忠義上
title.raw: 卷一百八十七上 列傳第一百三十七上: 忠義上 Volume 187 Biographies 137: Loyal and Righteous 1

sentences.zh: 女子稟陰柔之質，有從人之義。

translations.literal: Women receive the quality of yin softness and possess the principle of following others.
translations.idiomatic: Women are endowed with a gentle, yielding nature and carry the obligation to defer to others.

sentences.zh: 前代誌貞婦烈女，蓋善其能以禮自防。

translations.literal: Former ages recorded chaste wives and heroic women, largely commending their ability to guard themselves through ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties recorded chaste wives and women of fierce integrity, chiefly to praise their ability to protect themselves through propriety.

sentences.zh: 至若失身賊庭，不汙非義；

translations.literal: As for those who lost their persons in the rebel court, not defiled by what was not righteous;
translations.idiomatic: Then there were those who fell into rebel hands yet were not stained by unrighteous conduct;

sentences.zh: 臨白刃而慷慨，誓丹衷而激發；

translations.literal: facing gleaming blades with fervor, vowing a loyal heart and stirred to ardor;
translations.idiomatic: who faced naked blades with resolute courage and pledged undying loyalty with passionate conviction;

sentences.zh: 粉身不顧，視死如歸，雖在壯夫，恐難守節，窈窕之操，不其賢乎！

translations.literal: disregarding their bodies shattered, viewing death as returning home—even stout men might find it hard to keep their integrity; the conduct of graceful women—is it not worthy?
translations.idiomatic: who gave their bodies without hesitation and embraced death as though going home—even sturdy men might struggle to match such constancy; are not such women's virtues truly admirable!

sentences.zh: 其次梁鴻之妻，無辭偕隱，共姜之誓，不踐二庭，婦道母儀，克彰圖史，又其長也。

translations.literal: Next, the wife of Liang Hong, without demurring shared seclusion; Gong Jiang's oath, not entering two courtyards—wifely conduct and maternal exemplars, able to shine forth in histories and annals; these are yet greater.
translations.idiomatic: Then there were exemplars such as the wife of Liang Hong, who shared her husband's seclusion without complaint, and Gong Jiang, who swore never to enter a second household—models of wifely duty and maternal virtue celebrated in the histories; these represent an even higher standard.

sentences.zh: 末代風靡，貞行寂寥，聊播椒蘭，以貽閨壺，彤管之職，幸無忽焉！

translations.literal: In the late age customs are dissipated, chaste conduct sparse; I briefly spread pepper and orchid, to leave for the inner quarters—the duty of the red brush, may it not be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: In these later times morals have declined and exemplary fidelity is rare; I offer these fragrant accounts for the women of the inner chambers—may those who record virtue in the histories not overlook them!

sentences.zh: 李德武妻裴氏李德武妻裴氏，字淑英，戶部尚書、安邑公矩之女也。

translations.literal: Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu—Pei Shi, styled Shuying, was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shi, wife of Li Dewu, was styled Shuying and was the daughter of Pei Ju, Director of the Household Ministry and Duke of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 性婉順有容德，事父母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Her nature was gentle and compliant, with a bearing of virtue; she served her parents and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and gracious in disposition, she was renowned for the filial devotion with which she served her parents.

sentences.zh: 適德武，經一年而德武坐從父金才事徙嶺表。

translations.literal: She married Dewu; after one year Dewu was exiled to Lingnan on account of his involvement in his cousin Jin Cai's affair.
translations.idiomatic: She married Li Dewu, but after only a year he was banished to Lingnan because of his cousin Jin Cai's case.

sentences.zh: 矩時為黃門侍郎，奏請德武離婚，煬帝許之。

translations.literal: Ju was then Vice Director of the Yellow Gate; he memorialized requesting that Dewu divorce, and Emperor Yang approved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Ju was Vice Director of the Yellow Gate; he petitioned for Li Dewu to divorce her, and Emperor Yang granted the request.

sentences.zh: 德武將與裴別，謂曰：「燕婉始爾，便事分離，方遠投瘴癘，恐無還理。

translations.literal: As Dewu was about to part from Pei, he said: "Our tender union has only just begun, yet we must separate; I am about to be cast far into malarial lands, and I fear there will be no returning.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Dewu was about to leave Pei, he said to her, "We have only just begun our life together, yet we must part; I am being sent far into the pestilential south, and I fear I shall never return.

sentences.zh: 尊君奏留，必欲改嫁耳，於此即事長訣矣！」

translations.literal: Your honored father has memorialized to keep you here; he surely intends you to remarry—here and now we take our long farewell!"
translations.idiomatic: Your father has petitioned to keep you here; he surely means for you to remarry—this is our final parting!"

sentences.zh: 裴泣而對曰：「婦人事夫，無再醮之禮。

translations.literal: Pei wept and replied: "A wife serves her husband; there is no ritual of marrying again.
translations.idiomatic: Pei wept and answered, "A wife serves her husband; there is no rite that permits a second marriage.

sentences.zh: 夫者，天也，何可背乎！

translations.literal: The husband is Heaven—how could one turn against him!
translations.idiomatic: A husband is like Heaven itself—how could I turn against him!

sentences.zh: 守之以死，必無他志！」

translations.literal: I shall guard this unto death; I shall certainly have no other intent!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall hold to this unto death; I will have no other thought!"

sentences.zh: 因操刀欲割耳自誓，保者禁之，乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon she took up a knife intending to cut off her ear in oath; her guardians restrained her, and she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: She then seized a knife to cut off her ear in pledge, but her attendants restrained her and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 裴與德武別後，容貌毀悴，常讀佛經，不御膏澤。

translations.literal: After Pei parted from Dewu, her appearance was wasted and haggard; she constantly read Buddhist sutras and did not use cosmetics.
translations.idiomatic: After she parted from Li Dewu, Pei's appearance withered with grief; she read Buddhist scriptures constantly and wore no cosmetics.

sentences.zh: 李氏之姊妹在都邑者，歲時朔望，必命左右致敬而省焉。

translations.literal: For the sisters of the Li clan who were in the capital, at the seasons and on the first and fifteenth of the month she always ordered her attendants to pay respects and inquire after them.
translations.idiomatic: For Li family sisters living in the capital, at each season and on the first and fifteenth of every month she always had her attendants pay respects and inquire after their welfare.

sentences.zh: 裴又嘗讀《烈女傳》，見稱述不改嫁者，乃謂所親曰：「不踐二庭，婦人常理，何為以此載於記傳乎？」

translations.literal: Pei had also once read the Biographies of Heroic Women and, seeing praise for those who did not remarry, said to those close to her: "Not entering two courtyards is ordinary conduct for a wife—why record such things in annals?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei had once read the Biographies of Heroic Women and, seeing accounts that praised women who refused remarriage, remarked to her intimates, "Never entering a second household is ordinary wifely conduct—why should such things be recorded in the histories?"

sentences.zh: 後十餘年間，與德武音信斷絕。

translations.literal: For more than ten years thereafter, correspondence with Dewu was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years afterward, all communication with Li Dewu ceased.

sentences.zh: 矩欲奪其志。

translations.literal: Ju wished to change her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju sought to change her mind.

sentences.zh: 時有柳直求婚，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zhi sought her hand in marriage, and he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a man named Liu Zhi sought her hand in marriage, and Ju consented.

sentences.zh: 期有定日，乃以翦刀斷其髮，悲泣絕粒。

translations.literal: When the wedding day was fixed, she cut off her hair with scissors, wept in grief, and stopped eating grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the wedding day was set, she cut off her hair with scissors, wept bitterly, and refused all food.

sentences.zh: 矩不可奪，乃止。

translations.literal: Ju could not change her mind, and so desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to sway her, Ju gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 德武已於嶺表娶爾硃氏為妻，及遇赦得還，至襄州，聞裴守節，乃出其後妻，重與裴合。

translations.literal: Dewu had already taken Erzhu Shi as wife in Lingnan; when he received an amnesty and returned, reaching Xiangzhou and hearing that Pei had kept her integrity, he sent away his later wife and reunited with Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dewu had meanwhile married a woman named Erzhu in the south; when an amnesty allowed him to return and he reached Xiangzhou, he learned that Pei had kept her chastity, dismissed his second wife, and took Pei back.

sentences.zh: 生三男四女。

translations.literal: They bore three sons and four daughters.
translations.idiomatic: They had three sons and four daughters.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，德武終於鹿城令，裴歲餘亦卒。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, Dewu died in office as magistrate of Lucheng; a little over a year later Pei also died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, Li Dewu died while serving as magistrate of Lucheng; a little more than a year later Pei died as well.

sentences.zh: 楊慶妻王氏楊慶妻王氏，世充兄之女也。

translations.literal: Wang Shi, wife of Yang Qing—Wang Shi was the daughter of Wang Shichong's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi, wife of Yang Qing, was the daughter of Wang Shichong's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 慶即隋河間王弘之子。

translations.literal: Qing was the son of Hong, Prince of Hejian of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing was a son of Hong, the Sui Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 大業末，封郇王，為滎陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xun and made Administrator of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xun and appointed Administrator of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 後陷於世充。

translations.literal: Later he fell into Shichong's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He later fell into Wang Shichong's power.

sentences.zh: 世充以兄女妻之，授管州刺史。

translations.literal: Shichong gave him his brother's daughter in marriage and appointed him Prefect of Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong gave him his niece in marriage and appointed him Prefect of Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 及太宗攻圍洛陽，慶謀背世充，欲與其妻俱來歸國。

translations.literal: When the Taizong besieged Luoyang, Qing plotted to turn against Shichong and wished to come over to the Tang together with his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong besieged Luoyang, Yang Qing plotted to defect from Wang Shichong and intended to bring his wife with him to surrender to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 妻謂慶曰：「鄭國以妾奉箕帚於公者，所以結公心耳。

translations.literal: His wife said to Qing: "The State of Zheng gave me to you with broom and dustpan to bind your heart.
translations.idiomatic: His wife said to him, "The Zheng state gave me to you in marriage to win your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今既二三其行，負恩背義，自為身謀，妾將奈何？

translations.literal: Now you have turned in two or three ways, betraying favor and turning against righteousness, scheming for yourself—what am I to do?
translations.idiomatic: Now you waver in your loyalty, betray your obligations, and plot only for yourself—what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 若至長安，則公家之婢耳！

translations.literal: If I reach Chang'an, I shall be merely your family's serving maid!
translations.idiomatic: If I go to Chang'an, I shall be nothing but a servant in your household!

sentences.zh: 願送至東都，公之惠也。」

translations.literal: I wish to be sent back to the Eastern Capital—that would be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: I ask only that you send me back to the Eastern Capital—that would be your kindness to me."

sentences.zh: 慶不聽。

translations.literal: Qing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing would not heed her.

sentences.zh: 伺慶出後，謂侍者曰：「唐兵若勝，我家則戚。

translations.literal: When Qing had gone out, she said to her attendants: "If the Tang troops prevail, our house will be kin to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After Qing had gone out, she told her attendants, "If the Tang forces win, our family will be counted among the enemy's kin.

sentences.zh: 鄭國無危，吾夫又死，進退維谷。

translations.literal: If the State of Zheng is not in peril, my husband will die; advance and retreat alike are a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: If the Zheng state is not endangered, my husband will die; whether I advance or retreat, I am trapped.

sentences.zh: 何以生焉？」

translations.literal: How could I go on living?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I go on living?"

sentences.zh: 乃飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: She then took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 慶既入朝，官至宜州刺史。

translations.literal: After Qing entered court service, he rose to Prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Qing entered Tang service, he rose to the post of Prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 時又有獨孤武都，謀叛王世充歸國，事覺誅死。

translations.literal: At the same time there was also Dugu Wudu, who plotted to rebel against Wang Shichong and return to the Tang; the affair was discovered and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dugu Wudu also plotted to defect from Wang Shichong to the Tang; when the plot was discovered he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 武都子師仁，年始三歲，世充以其年幼不殺，使禁掌之。

translations.literal: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Shichong, because he was young, did not kill him but had him confined and kept in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu's son Shiren was only three years old; Wang Shichong spared him because of his age and had him imprisoned under guard.

sentences.zh: 乳母王氏，號蘭英，請髡鉗，求入保養，世充許之。

translations.literal: His wet-nurse Wang Shi, called Lanying, requested to be shaved and shackled in order to enter and nurture him; Shichong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: His wet nurse Wang Shi, known as Lanying, asked to be shorn and shackled so she could enter the prison to care for him; Wang Shichong consented.

sentences.zh: 蘭英撫育提攜，備盡筋力。

translations.literal: Lanying reared and guided him, exhausting all her strength.
translations.idiomatic: Lanying raised and guided him, exhausting every ounce of her strength.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂年饑，人多鋨死，蘭英扶路乞丐捃拾。

translations.literal: At the time there was turmoil and famine year after year; many died of starvation; Lanying, supporting herself along the road, begged and gathered scraps.
translations.idiomatic: In those years of chaos and famine many starved to death; Lanying went begging along the roads to gather whatever she could find.

sentences.zh: 遇有所得，便歸與師仁；

translations.literal: whenever she obtained anything, she at once returned and gave it to Shiren;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever she obtained she brought back at once for Shiren;

sentences.zh: 蘭英唯啖土飲水而已。

translations.literal: Lanying herself ate only earth and drank only water.
translations.idiomatic: Lanying herself ate only scraps of earth and drank only water.

sentences.zh: 後詐采拾，乃竊師仁歸於京師。

translations.literal: Later, pretending to go gathering, she stole Shiren away and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later she pretended to go out gathering and secretly carried Shiren away to the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其義，下詔曰：「師仁乳母王氏，慈惠有聞，撫鞠無倦，提攜遺幼，背逆歸朝。

translations.literal: Gaozu commended her righteousness and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet-nurse Wang Shi is known for kindness and grace, rearing without weariness, guiding the orphaned infant, turning from rebellion to return to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised her conduct and issued an edict: "Shiren's wet nurse Wang Shi is renowned for kindness and grace; she reared him without rest, guided the orphaned child, and turned from rebellion to bring him back to the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 宜有褒隆，以錫其號。

translations.literal: She should receive commendation and elevation, and be granted a title.
translations.idiomatic: She deserves honor and elevation, and should be granted a title.

sentences.zh: 可封永壽郡君」。

translations.literal: She may be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Let her be enfeoffed as Lady of Yongshou Commandery."

sentences.zh: 楊三安妻李氏楊三安妻李氏，雍州涇陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an—Li Shi was a native of Jingyang in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, wife of Yang San'an, was a native of Jingyang in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事舅姑以孝聞。

translations.literal: She served her parents-in-law and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She was renowned for the filial devotion with which she served her parents-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及舅姑亡沒，三安亦死，二子孩童，家至貧窶。

translations.literal: When her parents-in-law died, San'an also died; the two sons were still children, and the household was utterly destitute.
translations.idiomatic: After her parents-in-law died, San'an died as well, leaving two young sons and a household in utter poverty.

sentences.zh: 李晝則力田，夜紡緝，數年間葬舅姑及夫之叔侄兄弟者七喪，深為遠近所嗟尚。

translations.literal: By day Li worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within several years she buried her parents-in-law and seven of her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers—deeply admired near and far.
translations.idiomatic: By day she worked the fields; by night she spun and wove; within a few years she had conducted seven funerals for her parents-in-law and her husband's uncles, nephews, and brothers, winning deep admiration throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而異之，賜帛二百段，遣州縣所在存恤之。

translations.literal: Taizong heard of it and marveled, bestowing two hundred bolts of silk and ordering the prefecture and county where she lived to provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of this he was deeply impressed, granted her two hundred bolts of silk, and ordered the local prefecture and county to provide for her welfare.

sentences.zh: 魏衡妻王氏魏衡妻王氏，梓州郪人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng—Wang Shi was a native of Qi in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi, wife of Wei Heng, was a native of Qi in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 武德初，薛仁杲舊將房企地侵掠梁郡，因獲王氏，逼而妻之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wude era, Fang Qidi, a former officer of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery and seized Wang Shi, forcing her to become his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, Fang Qidi, a former officer of Xue Rengao, raided Liang Commandery, captured Wang Shi, and forced her to marry him.

sentences.zh: 後企地漸強盛，衡謀以城應賊。

translations.literal: Later, as Qidi grew steadily stronger, Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As Fang Qidi grew stronger, Wei Heng plotted to surrender the city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 企地領眾將趨梁州，未至數十里，飲酒醉臥。

translations.literal: Qidi led his troops toward Liangzhou; when still several tens of li away, he drank wine and lay down drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qidi led his forces toward Liangzhou; when they were still several tens of li away, he drank himself into a stupor and fell asleep.

sentences.zh: 王氏取其佩刀斬之，攜其首入城，賊眾乃散。

translations.literal: Wang Shi took his belt knife and slew him, carrying his head into the city; the rebel host then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi took his belt knife and killed him, then carried his head into the city; the rebel force scattered.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，封為崇義夫人，舍衡同賊之罪。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased, enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi, and pardoned Heng's crime of colluding with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased, enfeoffed her as Lady of Chongyi, and pardoned Wei Heng for conspiring with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 樊會仁母敬氏樊會仁母敬氏，字像子，蒲州河東人也。

translations.literal: Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren—Jing Shi, styled Xiangzi, was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Shi, mother of Fan Huiren, was styled Xiangzi and was a native of Hedong in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十五，適樊氏，生會仁而夫喪，事舅姑姊姒以謹順聞。

translations.literal: At fifteen she married into the Fan clan, bore Huiren, and then her husband died; she served parents-in-law, sisters-in-law, and brothers' wives and was known for careful compliance.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen she married into the Fan family, bore Huiren, and was widowed; she served her parents-in-law and sisters-in-law with meticulous devotion and was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 及服終，母兄以其盛年，將奪其志。

translations.literal: When her mourning was complete, her mother and elder brother, because she was still in her prime, intended to change her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning period ended, her mother and elder brother, seeing that she was still young, sought to make her remarry.

sentences.zh: 微加諷諭，便悲恨嗚咽，如此者數四。

translations.literal: At the slightest hint of persuasion she would weep in grief and resentment; this happened four times.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest suggestion she would weep in grief and indignation; this happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 母兄乃潛許人為婚，矯稱母患以召之。

translations.literal: Her mother and brother then secretly betrothed her to another man and falsely claimed their mother was ill to summon her.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother and brother then secretly betrothed her to another man and summoned her home with a false report that their mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 凡所營具，皆寄之鄰里。

translations.literal: All the items prepared for the wedding were stored with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Everything prepared for the wedding was stored with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 像子既至，省母無疾，鄰家復具肴善，像子知為所欺，佯為不悟者。

translations.literal: When Xiangzi arrived and visited her mother, there was no illness; the neighbors again set out fine dishes—Xiangzi knew she had been deceived and pretended not to understand.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangzi arrived and found her mother was not ill, the neighbors had laid out a feast; realizing she had been tricked, she pretended not to notice.

sentences.zh: 其嫂復請像子沐浴。

translations.literal: Her sister-in-law again asked Xiangzi to bathe.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister-in-law then asked her to bathe.

sentences.zh: 像子私謂會仁曰：「吾不幸孀居，誓與汝父同穴。

translations.literal: Xiangzi privately told Huiren: "I am unfortunate in widowhood and have sworn to share a grave with your father.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi privately told Huiren, "I am unfortunate to be a widow and have sworn to share a grave with your father.

sentences.zh: 所以不死者，徒以我母羸老，汝身幼弱。

translations.literal: The reason I have not died is only that my mother is frail and aged and you are still young and weak.
translations.idiomatic: The only reason I have not died is that my mother is frail and aged and you are still young and helpless.

sentences.zh: 今汝舅欲奪吾志，將加逼迫，於汝何如！」

translations.literal: Now your uncle wishes to change my resolve and will force me—what will become of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Now your uncle means to force me to remarry—what will become of you then!"

sentences.zh: 會仁失聲啼泣。

translations.literal: Huiren burst out weeping aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Huiren burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 像子撫之曰：「汝勿啼。

translations.literal: Xiangzi comforted him: "Do not weep.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi comforted him and said, "Do not cry.

sentences.zh: 吾向偽不覺者，令汝舅不我為意。

translations.literal: I have been pretending not to understand so that your uncle would not take me into account.
translations.idiomatic: I have been pretending not to understand so your uncle would not be on his guard against me.

sentences.zh: 聞汝啼，知吾覺悟，必加妨備，則吾難為計矣！」

translations.literal: Hearing you weep, he will know I am aware and will surely increase his precautions—then I shall have no way to act!"
translations.idiomatic: If he hears you cry, he will know I have understood and will guard against me—then I shall have no way to escape!"

sentences.zh: 會仁便佯睡，像子於是伺隙攜之遁歸。

translations.literal: Huiren then pretended to sleep; Xiangzi thereupon seized an opening, took him, and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: Huiren then pretended to sleep; Xiangzi seized her chance, took him, and fled home.

sentences.zh: 中路，兄使追及之，將逼與俱返。

translations.literal: On the way her brother sent men to overtake them and was about to force them to return together.
translations.idiomatic: On the road her brother sent men to overtake them and tried to force them to return.

sentences.zh: 像子誓以必死，辭情甚切，其兄感嘆而止。

translations.literal: Xiangzi swore she would die; her words were most earnest, and her brother sighed in admiration and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzi swore she would die rather than submit; her words were so earnest that her brother sighed in admiration and let them go.

sentences.zh: 後會仁年十八病卒，時像子母已終。

translations.literal: Later, when Huiren was eighteen, he died of illness; by then Xiangzi's mother had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huiren was eighteen, he died of illness; by then Xiangzi's mother had already died.

sentences.zh: 既葬，像子謂其所親曰：「吾老母不幸，又夫死子亡，義無久活。」

translations.literal: After the burial, Xiangzi said to those close to her: "My old mother met misfortune, and now my husband is dead and my son is gone—by righteousness I cannot live long."
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral she told her intimates, "My mother met a sad end, and now my husband is dead and my son is gone—I have no right to go on living."

sentences.zh: 於是號慟不食，數日而死。

translations.literal: She then wailed in grief and stopped eating, and within several days died.
translations.idiomatic: She then wailed in grief, refused all food, and died within a few days.

sentences.zh: 絳州孝女衛氏絳州孝女衛氏，字無忌，夏縣人也。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter Wei of Jiangzhou—Wei Shi, styled Wuji, was a native of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Daughter Wei of Jiang Prefecture—Wei Shi, styled Wuji, was a native of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 初，其父為鄉人衛長則所殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, her father had been killed by a fellow townsman, Wei Changze.
translations.idiomatic: Her father had earlier been killed by a fellow townsman named Wei Changze.

sentences.zh: 無忌年六歲，母又改嫁，無兄弟。

translations.literal: Wuji was six years old; her mother remarried, and she had no brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was six at the time; her mother remarried, and she had no brothers.

sentences.zh: 及長，常思復仇。

translations.literal: When she grew up, she constantly thought of revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When she grew up, she constantly brooded on revenge.

sentences.zh: 無忌從伯常設宴為樂，長則時亦預坐，無忌以磚擊殺之。

translations.literal: Wuji's paternal uncle often held banquets for pleasure; Changze would sometimes also be present; Wuji killed him with a brick strike.
translations.idiomatic: Her paternal uncle often held feasts for pleasure, and Changze sometimes attended; Wuji struck him dead with a brick.

sentences.zh: 既而詣吏，稱父仇既報，請就刑戮。

translations.literal: Thereupon she went to the officials, declaring that her father's enemy had been avenged and asking to submit to execution.
translations.idiomatic: She then went to the authorities, declared that her father's murder had been avenged, and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 巡察大使、黃門侍郎褚遂良以聞，太宗嘉其孝烈，特令免罪，給傳乘徙於雍州，並給田宅，仍令州縣以禮嫁之。

translations.literal: The touring inspector, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Chu Suiliang reported it; Taizong commended her filial heroism, specially ordered her pardoned, provided relay horses to move her to Yongzhou, and also granted fields and a residence, further ordering the prefecture and county to marry her off with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The touring inspector, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Chu Suiliang reported the case; Emperor Taizong praised her filial courage, specially pardoned her, provided relay horses to relocate her to Yong Prefecture, granted her fields and a residence, and ordered the local authorities to arrange a proper marriage for her.

sentences.zh: 濮州孝女賈氏孝女賈氏，濮州鄄城人也。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter Jia of Puzhou—the Filial Daughter Jia was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Daughter Jia of Pu Prefecture was a native of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 年始十五，其父為宗人玄基所害。

translations.literal: When she was only fifteen, her father was killed by a clansman, Xuanji.
translations.idiomatic: When she was only fifteen, her father was killed by a clansman named Xuanji.

sentences.zh: 其弟強仁年幼，賈氏撫育之，誓以不嫁。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Qiangren was still young; Jia reared him and swore not to marry.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Qiangren was still a child; Jia raised him and swore never to marry.

sentences.zh: 及強仁成童，思共報復，乃俟玄基殺之；

translations.literal: When Qiangren reached boyhood, they thought together of revenge; they waited for Xuanji and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: When Qiangren came of age, they plotted revenge together; they lay in wait for Xuanji and killed him;

sentences.zh: 取其心肝，以祭父墓。

translations.literal: took his heart and liver, and used them to sacrifice at their father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: cut out his heart and liver and offered them at their father's grave.

sentences.zh: 遣強仁自列於縣，司斷以極刑。

translations.literal: They sent Qiangren to present himself at the county office; the authorities sentenced him to the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Qiangren to surrender himself at the county seat; the authorities sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 賈氏詣闕自陳己為，請代強仁死。

translations.literal: Jia went to the palace gates to declare herself culpable and asked to die in Qiangren's place.
translations.idiomatic: Jia went to court to confess her own guilt and asked to die in her brother's place.

sentences.zh: 高宗哀之，特下制賈氏及強仁免罪，移其家於洛陽。

translations.literal: Gaozong pitied her and specially issued an edict pardoning Jia and Qiangren and moving their household to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong was moved and specially pardoned both Jia and Qiangren, relocating their family to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭義宗妻盧氏鄭義宗妻盧氏，幽州范陽人，盧彥衡之女也。

translations.literal: Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong—Lu Shi was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, daughter of Lu Yanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shi, wife of Zheng Yizong, was a native of Fanyang in You Prefecture and daughter of Lu Yanheng.

sentences.zh: 略涉書史，事舅姑甚得婦道。

translations.literal: She had some acquaintance with books and histories; in serving her parents-in-law she thoroughly fulfilled wifely conduct.
translations.idiomatic: She had some education in history and literature and served her parents-in-law with exemplary wifely devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜有強盜數十人，持杖鼓噪，逾垣而入，家人悉奔竄，唯有姑獨在室。

translations.literal: Once at night several tens of robbers, holding staves and making a din, climbed over the wall and entered; the family all fled in panic, and only the mother-in-law remained alone in the room.
translations.idiomatic: One night several dozen robbers, armed with clubs and making a great racket, climbed over the wall; the whole household fled in terror, leaving only her mother-in-law alone in the room.

sentences.zh: 盧冒白刃往至姑側，為賊捶擊之，幾至於死。

translations.literal: Lu braved the gleaming blades and went to her mother-in-law's side; the robbers beat her and she nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Lu braved the robbers' blades to reach her mother-in-law's side; they beat her nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 賊去後，家人問曰：「群兇擾橫，人盡奔逃，何獨不懼？」

translations.literal: After the robbers left, the family asked: "When the violent ruffians were running wild, everyone fled—why alone were you unafraid?"
translations.idiomatic: After the robbers left, her family asked, "When those violent men were rampaging, everyone fled—why were you alone unafraid?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「人所以異於禽獸者，以其仁義也。

translations.literal: She replied: "What distinguishes humans from birds and beasts is their benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "What distinguishes human beings from birds and beasts is benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 昔宋伯姬守義赴火，流稱至今。

translations.literal: In antiquity Lady Bo Ji of Song upheld righteousness and went into the fire; her fame flows to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Lady Bo Ji of Song upheld righteousness and walked into the flames; her fame endures to this day.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不敏，安敢忘義！

translations.literal: Though I am not clever, how could I dare forget righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not clever, how could I dare abandon righteousness!

sentences.zh: 且鄰里有急，尚相赴救，況在於姑，而可委棄！

translations.literal: Moreover, when neighbors are in distress, one still rushes to help—how much more when it concerns one's mother-in-law, and one could abandon her!
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors are in distress, people still rush to help—how much more when it is one's mother-in-law, and one could abandon her!

sentences.zh: 若萬一危禍，豈宜獨生！」

translations.literal: If by chance there were danger and calamity, how could one live on alone!
translations.idiomatic: If disaster should strike, how could one live on alone!"

sentences.zh: 其姑每嘆云：「古人稱歲寒然後知松柏之後雕也，吾今乃知盧新婦之心矣！」

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law often sighed: "The ancients said that only in bitter cold does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither—I now know the heart of my new daughter-in-law Lu!"
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law often sighed, "The ancients said that only in bitter cold does one know the pine and cypress are last to wither—I now know the heart of my daughter-in-law Lu!"

sentences.zh: 貞觀中卒。

translations.literal: She died during the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: She died during the Zhenguan reign.

sentences.zh: 劉寂妻夏侯氏劉寂妻夏侯氏，滑州胙城人，字碎金。

translations.literal: Xiahou Shi, wife of Liu Ji—Xiahou Shi was a native of Zuocheng in Huazhou, styled Suijin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shi, wife of Liu Ji, was a native of Zuocheng in Hua Prefecture and was styled Suijin.

sentences.zh: 父長雲，為鹽城縣丞，因疾喪明。

translations.literal: Her father Changyun was Assistant Magistrate of Yancheng and lost his sight from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Changyun served as Assistant Magistrate of Yancheng and went blind from illness.

sentences.zh: 碎金乃求離其夫，以終侍養。

translations.literal: Suijin then sought to leave her husband in order to devote herself entirely to caring for him.
translations.idiomatic: Suijin then sought to leave her husband so she could devote herself entirely to caring for him.

sentences.zh: 經十五年，兼事後母，以至孝聞。

translations.literal: For fifteen years she also served her stepmother and was known for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: For fifteen years she also cared for her stepmother and was renowned for utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及父卒，毀瘠殆不勝喪，被髮徒跣，負土成墳，廬於墓側，每日一食，如此者積年。

translations.literal: When her father died, she was so wasted by grief she could scarcely bear the mourning; with hair unbound and barefoot, she carried earth to build the tomb and lived in a hut beside the grave, eating only one meal a day, for years.
translations.idiomatic: When her father died, grief left her so emaciated she could scarcely endure the mourning; with hair unbound and barefoot, she carried earth to build the tomb, lived in a hut beside the grave, and ate only one meal a day for years.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，有制表其門閭，賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, an edict was issued to honor her gate and lane, granting grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, an edict honored her household and granted her grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 楚王靈龜妃上官氏楚王靈龜妃上官氏，秦州上邽人。

translations.literal: Shangguan Shi, consort of Prince Lingui of Chu—Shangguan Shi was a native of Shanggui in Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Shi, consort of Prince Lingui of Chu, was a native of Shanggui in Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父懷仁，右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Her father Huairen was General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Huairen was a general of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 上官年十八，歸於靈龜，繼楚哀王後。

translations.literal: When Shangguan was eighteen she married Lingui, succeeding after the lamented King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Shangguan married Prince Lingui, succeeding as consort after the lamented King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 本生具存，朝夕侍奉，恭謹彌甚。

translations.literal: Her birth parents were still alive; morning and evening she attended them, her respect and care ever increasing.
translations.idiomatic: Her birth parents were still alive; morning and evening she attended them with ever-increasing respect and care.

sentences.zh: 凡有新味，非舅姑啖訖，未曾先嘗。

translations.literal: Whenever there was some new delicacy, unless her parents-in-law had finished tasting it, she never tasted it first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there was a new delicacy, she never tasted it until her parents-in-law had finished.

sentences.zh: 經數載，靈龜薨。

translations.literal: After several years Lingui died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Prince Lingui died.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，其前妃閻氏，嫁不逾年而卒，又無近族，眾議欲不舉之。

translations.literal: When he was about to be buried, his former consort Lady Yan, who had married less than a year before dying and had no close kin, the assembly debated not conducting her funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be buried, his former consort Lady Yan had married less than a year before dying and had no close kin; the assembly debated whether to bury her at all.

sentences.zh: 上官氏曰：「必神而靈，寧可使孤魂無托！」

translations.literal: Shangguan said: "If spirits are divine and numinous, how could one let a solitary soul have no resting place!"
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan said, "If the dead retain consciousness, how could we leave a solitary soul without a resting place!"

sentences.zh: 於是備禮同葬，聞者莫不嘉嘆。

translations.literal: She then prepared full rites and buried her together; all who heard of it sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: She prepared full rites and buried her with him; all who heard sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 服終，諸兄姊謂曰：「妃年尚少，又無所生，改醮異門，禮儀常範，妃可思之。」

translations.literal: When her mourning ended, her elder brothers and sisters said: "The consort is still young and bore no children; to remarry into another house is ordinary ritual propriety—the consort should consider it.
translations.idiomatic: When her mourning ended, her siblings said, "You are still young and bore no children; remarriage is ordinary custom—you should consider it.

sentences.zh: 妃掩泣對曰：「丈夫以義烈標名，婦人以守節為行。

translations.literal: The consort covered her face and wept, replying: "A husband makes his name through righteous heroism; a wife makes her conduct through keeping integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Covering her face, she wept and replied, "A husband wins renown through righteous courage; a wife wins it through steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 未能即先犬馬，以殉溝壑，寧可復飾妝服，有他志乎！」

translations.literal: I have not yet been able to go before the hounds and horses and follow them into the ditch—how could I again adorn myself in dress and have another intent!
translations.idiomatic: I have not yet been able to follow my husband into the grave—how could I adorn myself again and turn to another man!

sentences.zh: 遽將刀截鼻割耳以自誓，諸兄姊知其志不可奪，嘆息而止。

translations.literal: She at once took a knife and cut off her nose and ear in oath; her siblings, knowing her resolve could not be changed, sighed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: She immediately took a knife and cut off her nose and ear in pledge; her siblings, seeing her resolve could not be changed, sighed and gave up.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 楊紹宗妻王氏楊紹宗妻王氏，華州華陰人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shi, wife of Yang Shaozong—Wang Shi was a native of Huayin in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi, wife of Yang Shaozong, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，年二歲，所生母亡，為繼母鞠養。

translations.literal: At first, when she was two years old, her birth mother died and she was reared by her stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: When she was two her birth mother died and she was raised by her stepmother.

sentences.zh: 至年十五，父又征遼而歿。

translations.literal: By the age of fifteen her father also died on the Liaodong campaign.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen her father had also died on the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 繼母尋亦卒。

translations.literal: Her stepmother soon died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Her stepmother soon died as well.

sentences.zh: 王乃收所生及繼母屍柩，並立父形像，招魂遷葬訖，廬於墓側，陪其祖父母及父母墳。

translations.literal: Wang then gathered the coffins of her birth mother and stepmother, set up her father's portrait, summoned his soul and reburied him, and built a mourning hut beside the tomb, attending the graves of her grandparents and parents.
translations.idiomatic: Wang gathered the coffins of her birth mother and stepmother, set up her father's portrait, summoned his soul for reburial, and built a mourning hut beside the tomb to attend her grandparents and parents.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，詔曰：「故楊紹宗妻王氏，因心為孝，率性成道。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era an edict said: "The late Yang Shaozong's wife Wang Shi, with her heart made filial and her nature formed in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign an edict said, "The late Yang Shaozong's wife Wang Shi, filial in heart and steadfast in nature.

sentences.zh: 年迫桑榆，筋力衰謝。

translations.literal: Her years approach the mulberry and elm; her sinews and strength decline.
translations.idiomatic: Her years approach old age and her strength declines.

sentences.zh: 以往在隋朝，父歿遼左，招魂遷葬，負土成墳，又葬其祖父母等，遏此老年，親加板築。

translations.literal: Formerly during the Sui, when her father died in Liaodong, she summoned his soul for reburial and carried earth to build the tomb; she also buried her grandparents and the like—at this advanced age she personally added the boards and earth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui, when her father died in Liaodong, she summoned his soul for reburial and built his tomb by hand; she also buried her grandparents—and now in her old age she still personally worked the earth.

sentences.zh: 痛結晨昏，哀感行路。

translations.literal: Her grief bound morning and evening; her sorrow moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Her grief bound morning and evening; her sorrow moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 永言志行，嘉尚良深。

translations.literal: Speaking always of her will and conduct, the court admired her deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The court spoke always of her will and conduct with deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 宜標其門閭，用旌敏德。」

translations.literal: Her gate and lane should be marked to honor her keen virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Her household should be honored to commend her keen virtue."

sentences.zh: 賜物三十段、粟五十石。

translations.literal: She was granted thirty lengths of goods and fifty piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted thirty lengths of goods and fifty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 于敏直妻張氏于敏直妻張氏，營州都督、皖城公儉之女也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi, wife of Yu Minzhi—Zhang Shi was the daughter of Jian, Regional Commander of Yingzhou and Duke of Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi, wife of Yu Minzhi, was the daughter of Jian, Regional Commander of Yingzhou and Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 數歲時父母權有疾，即觀察顏色，不離左右，晝夜省侍，宛若成人。

translations.literal: When she was several years old and her parents were temporarily ill, she observed their countenance and never left their side, attending day and night like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: When she was a child and her parents fell ill, she watched their faces and never left their side, attending day and night like an adult.

sentences.zh: 及稍成長，恭順彌甚。

translations.literal: When she grew somewhat older, her respectful compliance grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: As she grew older, her respectful devotion only increased.

sentences.zh: 適延壽公於欽明子敏直。

translations.literal: She married the Duke of Yanshou, son of Qinming, to Minzhi.
translations.idiomatic: She married Yu Minzhi, son of Qinming, Duke of Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 初聞儉有疾，便即號踴自傷，期於必死。

translations.literal: When she first heard that Jian was ill, she at once wailed and injured herself, resolved to die.
translations.idiomatic: When she first heard Jian was ill, she wailed and injured herself, resolved to die with him.

sentences.zh: 儉卒後，兇問至，號哭一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When news of Jian's death arrived, she cried out once in grief and expired.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Jian's death arrived, she cried out once and died.

sentences.zh: 高宗下詔，賜物百段，仍令史官錄之。

translations.literal: Gaozong issued an edict granting her a hundred lengths of goods and ordering the historiographers to record it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong issued an edict granting her a hundred lengths of goods and ordered the historians to record her deed.

sentences.zh: 冀州女子王氏冀州鹿城女子王阿足者，早孤，無兄弟，唯姊一人。

translations.literal: Wang Azu of Lucheng in Jizhou—Wang Azu of Lucheng in Jizhou was orphaned early, had no brothers, and only one elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Azu of Lucheng in Ji Prefecture was orphaned early, had no brothers, and only one elder sister.

sentences.zh: 阿足初適同縣李氏，未有子而夫亡。

translations.literal: Azu first married a man of the same county, the Li clan; she had no children before her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: Azu first married a man of the same county surnamed Li; she had no children before her husband died.

sentences.zh: 時年尚少，人多聘之。

translations.literal: She was still young and many sought her hand in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: She was still young and many men sought her hand.

sentences.zh: 為姊年老孤寡，不能舍去，乃誓不嫁，以養其姊。

translations.literal: Because her sister was old, widowed, and alone, and she could not leave her, she swore not to marry and supported her sister.
translations.idiomatic: Because her sister was old, widowed, and alone, she could not abandon her; she swore not to marry and supported her sister instead.

sentences.zh: 每晝營田業，夜便紡績，衣食所須，無非阿足出者，如此二十餘年。

translations.literal: By day she worked the fields; by night she spun; all clothing and food came from Azu alone—for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: By day she worked the fields; by night she spun; for more than twenty years all food and clothing came from Azu alone.

sentences.zh: 及姊喪，葬送以禮。

translations.literal: When her sister died, she buried and sent her off with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When her sister died, she buried her with full rites.

sentences.zh: 鄉人莫不稱其節行，競令妻女求與相識。

translations.literal: Neighbors all praised her integrity; they eagerly had their wives and daughters seek her acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors praised her integrity; they eagerly had their wives and daughters seek her acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，竟終於家。

translations.literal: Several years later she finally died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later she died at home.

sentences.zh: 樊彥琛妻魏氏樊彥琛妻魏氏，楚州淮陰人。

translations.literal: Wei Shi, wife of Fan Yanchen—Wei Shi was a native of Huaiyin in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shi, wife of Fan Yanchen, was a native of Huaiyin in Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 彥琛病篤，將卒，魏泣而言曰：「幸以愚陋，托身明德，奉侍衣裳，二十餘載。

translations.literal: When Yanchen was gravely ill and about to die, Wei wept and said: "Fortunately, in my foolishness and lowliness, I entrusted myself to your bright virtue and attended your garments for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchen was gravely ill and near death, Wei wept and said, "Though I am foolish and lowly, I entrusted myself to your bright virtue and served you for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 豈意釁妨所招，遽見此禍。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that the offense I provoked would suddenly bring this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought the offense I provoked would suddenly bring this calamity.

sentences.zh: 同入黃泉，是其願也。」

translations.literal: To enter the yellow springs together—that is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: To enter the yellow springs with you—that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 彥琛答曰：「死生常道，無所多恨。

translations.literal: Yanchen replied: "Death and life are the constant Way; there is nothing much to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchen replied, "Death and life are the constant Way; there is little to regret.

sentences.zh: 君宜勉勵，養諸孤，使其成立。

translations.literal: You should strive on, rear the orphans, and help them reach maturity.
translations.idiomatic: You should strive on, rear our orphans, and help them grow to maturity.

sentences.zh: 若相從而死，適足貽累，非吾所取也。」

translations.literal: If you follow me in death, you would only add to the burden—that is not what I would choose.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow me in death, you would only add to their burden—that is not what I want.

sentences.zh: 彥琛卒後，屬李敬業之亂，乃為賊所獲。

translations.literal: After Yanchen died, during the turmoil of Li Jingye's rebellion, she was captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanchen died, during Li Jingye's rebellion, she was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊黨知其素解絲竹，逼令彈箏。

translations.literal: The rebel band knew she was skilled in silk and bamboo and forced her to play the zither.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels knew she was skilled in music and forced her to play the zither.

sentences.zh: 魏氏嘆曰：「我夫不幸亡歿，未能自盡，茍復偷生。

translations.literal: Wei sighed: "My husband met the misfortune of untimely death; I was unable to end my life and have lived on in degradation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sighed, "My husband died untimely; I was unable to follow him and have lived on in degradation.

sentences.zh: 今爾見逼管弦，豈非禍從手發耶？」

translations.literal: Now you force me to touch strings and pipes—is this not calamity issuing from the hand!
translations.idiomatic: Now you force me to touch strings and pipes—is this not calamity born from my own hands!

sentences.zh: 乃引刀斬指，棄之於地。

translations.literal: She then drew a knife and cut off her fingers, casting them on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: She drew a knife and cut off her fingers, casting them on the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊黨又欲妻之，魏以必死自固。

translations.literal: The rebels also wished to take her as wife; Wei held fast with the resolve to die.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also wished to take her as wife; Wei held firm with the resolve to die.

sentences.zh: 賊等忿怒，以刃加頸，語云：「若不從我，即當殞命。」

translations.literal: The rebels grew angry, put blades to her neck, and said: "If you do not obey us, you will perish at once.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew angry, put blades to her neck, and said, "If you do not obey us, you will die at once.

sentences.zh: 乃厲聲罵曰：「爾等狗盜，乃欲汙辱好人，今得速死，會我本志。」

translations.literal: She then cried out in a stern voice: "You dog-thieves wish to defile a good person—now I may die quickly; that fulfills my original intent."
translations.idiomatic: She cried out fiercely, "You dog-thieves wish to defile an honorable woman—now I may die quickly; that fulfills my intent."

sentences.zh: 賊乃斬之，聞者莫不傷惜。

translations.literal: The rebels then cut her down; all who heard grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels cut her down; all who heard grieved for her.

sentences.zh: 鄒保英妻奚氏鄒保英妻奚氏，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying—Xi Shi; her place of origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shi, wife of Zou Baoying; her place of origin is unknown.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天年，契丹賊李盡忠來寇平州。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebel Li Jinzhong came to raid Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitan rebel Li Jinzhong raided Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 保英時任刺史，領兵討擊。

translations.literal: Baoying was then Prefect and led troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Baoying was then prefect and led troops to repel them.

sentences.zh: 既而城孤援寡，勢將欲陷。

translations.literal: Soon the city was isolated with few reinforcements and the situation was about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city was isolated, reinforcements were few, and defeat seemed imminent.

sentences.zh: 奚氏乃率家僮及城內女丁相助固守。

translations.literal: Xi then led household retainers and the women of the city to help defend steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: Xi led household retainers and the women of the city to help defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊退，所司以聞，優制封為誠節夫人。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated, the authorities reported it; by special edict she was enfeoffed as Lady of Sincere Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels retreated, the authorities reported her deed; by special edict she was enfeoffed as Lady of Sincere Integrity.

sentences.zh: 時有古玄應妻高氏，亦能固守飛狐縣城，卒免為突厥所陷。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Xuanying's wife Gao Shi also was able to defend Feihu county seat steadfastly and ultimately escaped being captured by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Shi, wife of Gu Xuanying, also defended Feihu county seat and ultimately kept it from falling to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「頃屬默啜攻城，咸憂陷沒。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Recently Mo-ch'ueh attacked cities; all feared they would fall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Recently Mo-chueh besieged our cities and all feared they would fall.

sentences.zh: 丈夫固守，猶不能堅，婦人懷忠，不憚流矢；

translations.literal: Husbands defended steadfastly yet could not hold firm; women harbored loyalty and did not fear flying arrows;
translations.idiomatic: Men defended the walls yet could not hold; women harbored loyalty and did not fear flying arrows;

sentences.zh: 由茲感激，危城重安。

translations.literal: through this stirring emotion the perilous city was again made secure.
translations.idiomatic: through their stirring devotion the endangered city was saved.

sentences.zh: 如不褒升，何以獎勸！

translations.literal: If they are not praised and elevated, how may one encourage and guide!
translations.idiomatic: If such deeds are not honored, how can we encourage others!

sentences.zh: 古玄應妻可封為徇忠縣君。」

translations.literal: Gu Xuanying's wife may be enfeoffed as Lady of Xunzhong County.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xuanying's wife may be enfeoffed as Lady of Xunzhong County.

sentences.zh: 宋庭瑜妻魏氏宋庭瑜妻魏氏，定州鼓城人，隋著作郎彥泉之後也。

translations.literal: Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu—Wei Shi was a native of Gucheng in Dingzhou, descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shi, wife of Song Tingyu, was a native of Gucheng in Ding Prefecture, a descendant of the Sui Authoring Gentleman Yanquan.

sentences.zh: 世為山東士族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a Shandong gentry clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they were a Shandong gentry clan.

sentences.zh: 父克己，有詞學，則天時為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: Her father Keji had literary talent; during Wu Zetian's reign he was Vice Director of the Heavenly Office.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Keji was a man of letters; during Wu Zetian's reign he was Vice Director of the Heavenly Office.

sentences.zh: 魏氏善屬文。

translations.literal: Wei was skilled at composing literary texts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 先天中，庭瑜自司農少卿左遷涪州別駕。

translations.literal: During the Xiantian era Tingyu was demoted from Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries to Assistant Administrator of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian era Tingyu was demoted from Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries to Assistant Administrator of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏氏隨夫之任，中路作《南征賦》以敘志，詞甚典美。

translations.literal: Wei followed her husband to his post; midway she composed "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to express her intent—the language was very elegant and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Wei accompanied her husband to his post; en route she composed "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition" to express her intent in language of great elegance.

sentences.zh: 開元中，庭瑜累遷慶州都督。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu was repeatedly promoted to Regional Commander of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era Tingyu rose repeatedly to Regional Commander of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，中書令張說年少時為克己所重，魏氏恨其夫為外職，乃作書與說，敘亡父疇昔之事，並為庭瑜申理，乃錄《南征賦》寄說。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Yue was young, Keji had valued him highly; resenting that her husband held an outer post, Wei wrote to Yue recounting her late father's former dealings with him and pleading Tingyu's case, enclosing the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Yue was young, Keji had valued him; resenting her husband's exile, Wei wrote to Yue recounting her late father's dealings with him and pleading Tingyu's case, enclosing the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."

sentences.zh: 說嘆曰：「曹大家《東征》之流也。」

translations.literal: Yue sighed: "In the manner of Lady Cao's 'Eastern Expedition.'
translations.idiomatic: Yue sighed, "In the manner of Lady Cao's 'Eastern Expedition.'

sentences.zh: 庭瑜尋轉廣州都督，道病卒。

translations.literal: Tingyu was soon transferred to Regional Commander of Guangzhou and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyu was soon transferred to Regional Commander of Guangzhou and died of illness on the road.

sentences.zh: 魏氏旬日亦殞，時人莫不傷之。

translations.literal: Wei also died within ten days; at the time everyone grieved for them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei died within ten days as well; all who heard grieved for them.

sentences.zh: 崔繪妻盧氏崔繪妻盧氏，幽州范陽人也，為山東著姓。

translations.literal: Lu Shi, wife of Cui Hui—Lu Shi was a native of Fanyang in Youzhou, a prominent surname of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shi, wife of Cui Hui, was a native of Fanyang in You Prefecture and belonged to a prominent Shandong clan.

sentences.zh: 祖幼孫，常州刺史。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Yousun was Prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yousun served as Prefect of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父獻，有美名，則天時歷鸞臺侍郎、文昌左丞。

translations.literal: Her father Xian had a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xian enjoyed a fine reputation; during Wu Zetian's reign he served as Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace and Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 天授中為酷吏來俊臣所陷，左遷西鄉令而卒。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he was framed by the cruel official Lai Junchen, demoted to Magistrate of Xixiang, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was framed by the cruel official Lai Junchen, demoted to Magistrate of Xixiang, and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 繪早終，盧既年少，諸兄常欲嫁之。

translations.literal: Hui died young; Lu was still young, and her elder brothers often wished to marry her off.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hui died young; Lu was still young, and her elder brothers often wished to marry her off.

sentences.zh: 盧輒稱病固辭。

translations.literal: Lu repeatedly claimed illness and firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Lu repeatedly claimed illness and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 盧亡姊之夫李思沖，神龍初為工部侍郎，又求續親。

translations.literal: Lu's deceased elder sister's husband Li Sichong, in the Shenlong era became Vice Minister of Works, and again sought to renew the kin tie.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's deceased elder sister's husband Li Sichong, in the Shenlong era became Vice Minister of Works and again sought to marry her.

sentences.zh: 時思沖當朝美職，諸兄不之拒。

translations.literal: At the time Sichong held a handsome post at court, and her brothers did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sichong held an eminent post at court, and her brothers did not refuse.

sentences.zh: 將婚之夕，方以告盧；

translations.literal: On the eve of the wedding they were about to inform Lu;
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the wedding they were about to tell Lu;

sentences.zh: 盧又固辭不可，仍令人防其門。

translations.literal: Lu again firmly refused and could not be moved, and they still had people guard her door.
translations.idiomatic: Lu refused again and could not be moved, and they had people guard her door.

sentences.zh: 盧謂左右曰：「吾自誓久已定矣！」

translations.literal: Lu said to those beside her: "My oath has long been fixed!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu told her attendants, "My oath was fixed long ago!"

sentences.zh: 乃夜中出自竇中，奔歸崔氏，髮面盡為糞穢所汙。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night she went out through a hole in the wall and fled back to the Cui household; her hair and face were entirely fouled with filth.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the night she crawled out through a hole in the wall and fled back to the Cui household; her hair and face were fouled with filth.

sentences.zh: 宗族見者皆為之垂淚。

translations.literal: All of the clan who saw her wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw her in the clan wept for her.

sentences.zh: 因出家為尼，諸尼欽其操行，皆尊事之。

translations.literal: She then left the world to become a nun; the nuns admired her conduct and all honored her.
translations.idiomatic: She then became a nun; the other nuns admired her conduct and all honored her.

sentences.zh: 開元中，以老病而卒。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era she died of old age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era she died of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 奉天縣竇氏二女奉天縣竇氏二女伯娘、仲娘，雖長於村野，而幼有志操。

translations.literal: The two daughters of the Dou clan of Fengtian County—Elder Sister and Second Sister—though reared in the countryside, from youth had resolute will.
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of the Dou clan of Fengtian County—Elder Sister and Second Sister—though raised in the countryside, had resolute wills from youth.

sentences.zh: 住與邠州接界。

translations.literal: Their residence bordered Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their home bordered Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，草賊數千人，持兵刃入其村落行剽劫，聞二女有容色，姊年十九，妹年十六，藏於巖窟間。

translations.literal: In the Yongtai era several thousand grass-bandits, holding weapons, entered their village to plunder; hearing the two girls had beauty—the elder nineteen, the younger sixteen—they hid in a cave.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongtai era several thousand bandits armed with blades entered their village to plunder; hearing the two sisters were beautiful—the elder nineteen, the younger sixteen—they hid in a cave.

sentences.zh: 賊徒擬為逼辱，乃先曳伯娘出，行數十步，又曳仲娘出，賊相顧自慰。

translations.literal: The bandits intended to force and dishonor them; they first dragged out Elder Sister, went several tens of paces, then dragged out Second Sister; the bandits looked at one another in satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits meant to violate them; they first dragged out Elder Sister, went several tens of paces, then dragged out Second Sister; the bandits looked at one another with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 行臨深谷，伯娘曰：「我豈受賊汙辱！」

translations.literal: As they came to a deep ravine, Elder Sister said: "How could I suffer defilement by bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: As they came to a deep ravine, Elder Sister cried, "I will never suffer defilement by bandits!"

sentences.zh: 乃投之於谷。

translations.literal: She then cast herself into the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: She cast herself into the ravine.

sentences.zh: 賊方驚駭，仲娘又投於谷。

translations.literal: The bandits were startled in horror; Second Sister also cast herself into the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were horrified; Second Sister also cast herself into the ravine.

sentences.zh: 谷深數百尺，姊尋卒；

translations.literal: The ravine was several hundred feet deep; the elder sister died at once;
translations.idiomatic: The ravine was hundreds of feet deep; the elder sister died at once;

sentences.zh: 仲娘腳折面破，血流被體，氣絕良久而蘇，賊義之而去。

translations.literal: Second Sister's legs were broken and her face shattered, blood flowing over her body; she ceased breathing for a long time then revived; the bandits, moved by righteousness, left.
translations.idiomatic: Second Sister's legs were broken and her face shattered, blood covering her body; she stopped breathing for a long time then revived; the bandits, moved by her conduct, left.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹第五琦感其貞烈，奏之；

translations.literal: Jingzhao Prefect Diwu Qi, moved by their chaste heroism, memorialized it;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Prefect Diwu Qi, moved by their chaste courage, memorialized the case;

sentences.zh: 詔旌表門閭，長免丁役，二女葬事官給。

translations.literal: An edict marked their gate and lane, long exempted corvée labor, and the state provided their funerals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict honored their household, long exempted corvée labor, and the state provided their funerals.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹曹陸海著賦以美之。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Assistant Cao Luhai composed a rhapsody in their praise.

sentences.zh: 盧甫妻李氏原武尉盧甫妻李氏，隴西成紀人也。

translations.literal: Li Shi, wife of Lu Fu, Magistrate of Yuanwu—Li Shi was a native of Chengji in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, wife of Lu Fu, Magistrate of Yuanwu, was a native of Chengji in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父瀾，春任蘄縣令。

translations.literal: Her father Lan served as Magistrate of Qi in spring.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Lan served as Magistrate of Qi.

sentences.zh: 界內先有草賊二千餘人。

translations.literal: Within the district there were already more than two thousand grass-bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Within the district there were already more than two thousand bandits.

sentences.zh: 瀾挺身入賊，結以誠信，賊並降附，百姓復業者二百餘家。

translations.literal: Lan went in person among the bandits and bound them with sincerity and trust; the bandits all surrendered, and more than two hundred households of common people resumed their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Lan went in person among the bandits and won them with sincerity and trust; they all surrendered, and more than two hundred households resumed their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 時曹升任徐州刺史，知賊降，領兵掩襲。

translations.literal: At the time Cao Sheng was promoted to Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cao Sheng was Prefect of Xuzhou; learning the bandits had surrendered, he led troops in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 賊得脫後，入縣殺瀾。

translations.literal: After the bandits escaped, they entered the county and killed Lan.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits escaped, they entered the county and killed Lan.

sentences.zh: 瀾將被殺，從父弟渤，詣賊救瀾，請代兄死。

translations.literal: As Lan was about to be killed, his younger cousin Bo went to the bandits to save Lan and asked to die in his elder brother's place.
translations.idiomatic: As Lan was about to be killed, his younger cousin Bo went to the bandits to save him and asked to die in his brother's place.

sentences.zh: 瀾又請留弟，弟兄爭死。

translations.literal: Lan again asked to keep his younger brother; the brothers contended over who should die.
translations.idiomatic: Lan again asked to keep his younger brother; the brothers contended over who should die.

sentences.zh: 瀾女盧甫妻，又泣請代父死。

translations.literal: Lan's daughter, wife of Lu Fu, also wept and asked to die in her father's place.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's daughter, Lu Fu's wife, also wept and asked to die in her father's place.

sentences.zh: 並為賊所害，宣慰使、吏部侍郎李季卿以節義聞。

translations.literal: All were killed by the bandits; Pacification Commissioner and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing reported their integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: All were killed by the bandits; Pacification Commissioner and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing reported their integrity and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 又有尉氏尉王泛妻裴氏，儀王傅巨卿之女也。

translations.literal: There was also Pei Shi, wife of Wang Fan, Magistrate of Weishi—daughter of Juqing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Pei Shi, wife of Wang Fan, Magistrate of Weishi, daughter of Juqing, Tutor to the Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 素有容範，為賊所俘，賊逼之。

translations.literal: She always had a fine bearing and was captured by bandits who forced her.
translations.idiomatic: She had always been graceful in bearing and was captured by bandits who tried to force her.

sentences.zh: 裴曰：「吾衣冠之子，當死即死，終不茍全一命，受汙於賊。」

translations.literal: Pei said: "I am a child of the cap and gown; when I should die I die—I will never cling to life and suffer defilement by bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Pei said, "I am a child of the gentry; when I must die I die—I will never cling to life and be defiled by bandits."

sentences.zh: 賊脅之以兵，逼之以罵，裴堅力抗之。

translations.literal: The bandits threatened her with weapons and abused her with curses; Pei firmly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits threatened her with blades and cursed her; Pei resisted firmly.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，乃支解裴氏，至死不屈。

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry and dismembered Pei; to the end she did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits grew angry and dismembered her; to the end she did not yield.

sentences.zh: 季卿亦以狀跡聞。

translations.literal: Jiqing also reported the facts to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqing also reported the facts to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「鄭州原武縣尉盧甫亡妻李氏、汴州尉氏縣尉王泛亡妻裴氏等，懿範傳家，柔明植性；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Li Shi, late wife of Lu Fu, Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zhengzhou, and Pei Shi, late wife of Wang Fan, Magistrate of Weishi in Bianzhou, and the like—exemplary conduct handed down in their families, gentle clarity planted in their natures;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Li Shi, late wife of Lu Fu, Magistrate of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture, and Pei Shi, late wife of Wang Fan, Magistrate of Weishi in Bian Prefecture, and the like—exemplary conduct in their families, gentle clarity in their natures;

sentences.zh: 頃因寇難，克彰義烈。

translations.literal: Recently, amid bandit calamity, they displayed righteous heroism.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, amid bandit calamity, they displayed righteous heroism.

sentences.zh: 或請代父死，表因心之孝；

translations.literal: Some asked to die in their father's place, showing the filial piety that springs from the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Some asked to die in their father's place, showing filial piety from the heart;

sentences.zh: 或誓逐夫亡，標難奪之節。

translations.literal: some swore to follow their husbands in death, marking integrity that could not be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: some swore to follow their husbands in death, marking integrity that could not be wrested away.

sentences.zh: 宜膺贈律，俾光休美。

translations.literal: They should receive posthumous honors to make their fine virtue shine.
translations.idiomatic: They should receive posthumous honors to make their fine virtue shine.

sentences.zh: 李氏可贈孝昌縣君，裴氏可贈河東縣君，仍編入史冊。」

translations.literal: Li Shi may be granted the title Lady of Xiaochang County; Pei Shi may be granted Lady of Hedong County; both are to be entered in the historical records."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi may be granted Lady of Xiaochang County; Pei Shi may be granted Lady of Hedong County; both are to be entered in the historical records."

sentences.zh: 瀾、渤亦贈官秩。

translations.literal: Lan and Bo were also granted official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Lan and Bo were also granted official ranks.

sentences.zh: 鄒待徵妻簿氏鄒待徵妻簿氏。

translations.literal: Bo Shi, wife of Zou Daizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Shi, wife of Zou Daizheng.

sentences.zh: 待徵，大歷中為常州江陰縣尉，其妻為海賊所掠。

translations.literal: Daizheng, in the Dali era, was Assistant Magistrate of Jiangyin in Changzhou; his wife was seized by sea pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Daizheng, in the Dali era, was Assistant Magistrate of Jiangyin in Chang Prefecture; his wife was seized by pirates.

sentences.zh: 薄氏守節，出待徵官誥於懷中，托付村人，使謂待徵曰：「義不受辱。」

translations.literal: Bo Shi kept her integrity, took Daizheng's official patent from her bosom, entrusted it to a village man, and had him tell Daizheng: "By righteousness I will not suffer dishonor."
translations.idiomatic: Bo Shi kept her integrity, took Daizheng's official patent from her bosom, entrusted it to a villager, and had him tell Daizheng, "By righteousness I will not suffer dishonor."

sentences.zh: 乃投江而死。

translations.literal: She then cast herself into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then cast herself into the river and died.

sentences.zh: 賊退潮落，待徵於江岸得妻屍焉。

translations.literal: When the bandits retreated and the tide fell, Daizheng found his wife's corpse on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates retreated and the tide fell, Daizheng found his wife's corpse on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 江左文士，多著節婦文以紀之。

translations.literal: Literary men of the lower Yangtze composed many essays on chaste wives to record her.
translations.idiomatic: Literary men of the lower Yangtze composed many essays on chaste wives to record her deed.

sentences.zh: 李湍妻李湍妻。

translations.literal: The wife of Li Tuan.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Li Tuan.

sentences.zh: 湍，吳元濟之軍人也。

translations.literal: Tuan was a soldier in Wu Yuanji's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was a soldier in Wu Yuanji's army.

sentences.zh: 元和中，淮南未平，湍心懷向順，乃急渡溵河，東降烏重胤。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era the Huainan region was not yet pacified; Tuan harbored thoughts of turning to the Tang and urgently crossed the Qin River to surrender east to Wu Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Huainan was not yet pacified; Tuan wished to defect to the Tang and urgently crossed the Qin River to surrender to Wu Zhongyin.

sentences.zh: 其妻遂為賊束縛在樹，臠而食之，至死，叫其夫曰：「善事烏僕射。」

translations.literal: His wife was then bound by the bandits to a tree, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband: "Serve Vice Censor Wu well."
translations.idiomatic: His wife was then bound to a tree by the rebels, cut apart, and eaten; to the end she called to her husband, "Serve Vice Censor Wu well."

sentences.zh: 觀者義之。

translations.literal: Those who watched were moved by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who watched were moved by her conduct.

sentences.zh: 至是，重胤以其事請列史冊。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongyin requested on the strength of the affair that it be entered in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyin then requested that her deed be entered in the historical records.

sentences.zh: 十三年，憲宗下詔從之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Emperor Xianzong issued an edict granting the request.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Emperor Xianzong issued an edict granting the request.

sentences.zh: 董昌齡母楊氏董昌齡母楊氏。

translations.literal: Yang Shi, mother of Dong Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shi, mother of Dong Changling.

sentences.zh: 昌齡常為泗州長史，世居於蔡。

translations.literal: Changling often served as Chief Administrator of Sizhou and for generations dwelt in Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Changling often served as Chief Administrator of Si Prefecture and his family had dwelt in Cai for generations.

sentences.zh: 少孤，受訓於母。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he received instruction from his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was instructed by his mother.

sentences.zh: 累事吳少誠、少陽，至元濟時，為吳房令。

translations.literal: He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wu Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wu Shaocheng and Shaoyang in succession; by Wu Yuanji's time he was Magistrate of Wufang.

sentences.zh: 楊氏潛誡曰：「逆順之理，成敗可知，汝宜圖之。」

translations.literal: Yang secretly admonished him: "The principle of rebellion and submission—success and failure can be known; you should plan for it."
translations.idiomatic: Yang secretly admonished him, "The logic of rebellion and loyalty—success and failure can be foreseen; you should plan accordingly."

sentences.zh: 昌齡志未果，元濟又署為郾城令。

translations.literal: Changling's resolve was not yet fulfilled; Yuanji again appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's resolve was not yet firm; Yuanji again appointed him Magistrate of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 楊氏復誡曰：「逆黨欺天，天所不福。

translations.literal: Yang again admonished: "Rebel bands deceive Heaven; Heaven will not bless them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang admonished again, "Rebel bands defy Heaven; Heaven will not bless them.

sentences.zh: 汝當速降，無以前敗為慮，無以老母為念。

translations.literal: You should surrender quickly; do not worry over past failures, and do not think of your old mother.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender quickly; do not worry over past failures, and do not think of your old mother.

sentences.zh: 汝為忠臣，吾雖歿無恨矣！」

translations.literal: If you become a loyal subject, though I die I shall have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: If you become a loyal subject, though I die I shall have no regret!"

sentences.zh: 及王師逼郾城，昌齡乃以城降，且說賊將鄧懷金歸款於李光顏。

translations.literal: When the imperial army pressed Yancheng, Changling then surrendered the city and also persuaded the rebel general Deng Huaijin to submit to Li Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army pressed Yancheng, Changling surrendered the city and persuaded the rebel general Deng Huaijin to submit to Li Guangyan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗聞之喜，急召昌齡至闕，直授郾城令、兼監察御史，仍賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and Acting Investigating Censor, also granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong heard with joy and urgently summoned Changling to court, directly appointing him Magistrate of Yancheng and Acting Investigating Censor, and granting the scarlet robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 昌齡泣謝曰：「此皆老母之訓。」

translations.literal: Changling wept and thanked him: "This is all my old mother's instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Changling wept and thanked him, "This is all my old mother's instruction."

sentences.zh: 憲宗嗟嘆良久。

translations.literal: Xianzong sighed in admiration for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong sighed in admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 元濟囚楊氏，欲殺之，而止者數矣。

translations.literal: Yuanji imprisoned Yang and wished to kill her, but several times was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji imprisoned Yang and wished to kill her, but was stopped several times.

sentences.zh: 蔡平，楊氏幸無恙，

translations.literal: When Cai was pacified, Yang fortunately remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was pacified, Yang fortunately remained unharmed.

sentences.zh: 陳許節度使李遜疏楊氏之強明節義以聞，乃封北平郡太君。

translations.literal: Chenxu Military Governor Li Xun memorialized Yang's strength, clarity, integrity, and righteousness; she was then enfeoffed as Senior Lady of Beiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu Military Governor Li Xun memorialized Yang's strength, clarity, integrity, and righteousness; she was then enfeoffed as Senior Lady of Beiping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 韋雍妻蘭陵縣君蕭氏韋雍妻蕭氏。

translations.literal: Xiao Shi, Lady of Lanling Commandery, wife of Wei Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Shi, Lady of Lanling Commandery, wife of Wei Yong.

sentences.zh: 雍，故太子賓客。

translations.literal: Yong was formerly Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was formerly Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 張弘靖鎮幽州日，奏授觀察判官，攝監察御史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed him Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hongjing governed Youzhou, he memorialized and appointed Yong Observation Aide, acting as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時屬朝廷制置未備，幽州俗本兇悍，尤不樂文儒為主帥，賓佐習於常態，忿其變通，議論不密，卒然起亂。
